questions.question: Which part of India did the Nizams of Asafjahi dynasty rule?
questions.solution:
• Asafjahi Nizams: Deccan provinces
  • History: The Nizams ruled the Hyderabad State in the Deccan, which was once the premier princely state of British India.

questions.question: Who was the Governor-General of Bengal when the Permanent Settlement was introduced there in 1793?
questions.solution:
• Governor-General 1793: Lord Cornwallis
  • Settlement: He introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, which turned zamindars into hereditary owners of the land.

questions.question: Who founded the famous Vikramashila University in the ninth century?
questions.solution:
• Vikramashila University: Dharmapala
  • Pala Dynasty: Founded in the 9th century, this was a premier Buddhist learning center that rivaled Nalanda in its prime.

questions.question: Who among the following travellers came to India from Uzbekistan in the 11th century?
questions.solution:
• Al-Biruni: Al-Biruni
  • Scholar: Coming from Uzbekistan (Khwarizm) with Mahmud of Ghazni, he wrote Kitab-ul-Hind, a deep study of Indian culture.

questions.question: Where is the Rumi Darwaza located?
questions.solution:
• Rumi Darwaza: Lucknow
  • Architecture: This magnificent gateway was built by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula in 1784 as part of the Bara Imambara complex.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers belonged to the Tuluva dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Tuluva Dynasty: Krishnadeva Raya
  • Vijayanagara: Krishnadeva Raya was the greatest ruler of the Tuluva dynasty and oversaw the empire's golden age.

questions.question: Who was the Nawab of Bhopal that ruled from 1868 to 1901?
questions.solution:
• Bhopal Ruler: Shah Jahan Begum
  • History: One of the famous Begums of Bhopal, she was a great patron of architecture and helped build the Taj-ul-Masajid.

questions.question: Which modern-day Indian state was created on 1 April 1937 as the United Provinces by the Britishers?
questions.solution:
• United Provinces: Uttar Pradesh
  • Name Change: The British created the United Provinces in 1937, which was renamed Uttar Pradesh after independence in 1950.

questions.question: The Battle of Bedara was fought between the British Army and the Dutch Army in:
questions.solution:
• Battle of Bedara: 1759
  • Outcome: This battle crushed Dutch ambitions in India, leaving the British East India Company without major European rivals in Bengal.

questions.question: After over 21 years stay in South Africa, Gandhiji returned to India in ______.
questions.solution:
• Gandhi's Return: 1915
  • Fact: Gandhi returned to India on 9th January 1915, a day now celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.question: In which year was the Bombay Stock Exchange established?
questions.solution:
• BSE Establishment: 1875
  • Economy: The Bombay Stock Exchange is the oldest stock exchange in Asia, originally starting under a banyan tree.

questions.question: Which of the following is a replica of the famous Taj Mahal built in 1679?
questions.solution:
• Bibi ka Maqbara: Bibi ka Maqbara
  • Architecture: Built by Prince Azam Shah in memory of his mother Dilras Banu Begum, it is often called the 'Taj of the Deccan.'

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Indian National Congress make the demand for a Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
• Constituent Assembly: 1934
  • Detail: The idea was first proposed by M.N. Roy in 1934, and the INC officially demanded it later that same year.

questions.question: The Indian Mutiny of 1857 effectively ended in the city of ______.
questions.solution:
• End of Mutiny: Gwalior
  • 1858: The fall of Gwalior and the death of Rani Lakshmibai in June 1858 marked the practical end of the widespread uprising.

questions.question: Who among the following had authored ‘Buddha Gaya: The Hermitage of Sakya Muni’ in 1878?
questions.solution:
• Archaeologist: Rajendralala Mitra
  • Fact: He was the first modern Indian indologist and archaeologist, known for his scholarly works on ancient Indian sites.

questions.question: Who among the following begun his excavations at Dholavira in 1990?
questions.solution:
• Dholavira Excavator: RS Bisht
  • Harappan Site: R.S. Bisht led the excavations that revealed Dholavira's unique water management system and tri-partite city planning.

questions.question: Who among the following was responsible for the partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.solution:
• Partition of Bengal: Lord Curzon
  • 1905: Curzon partitioned Bengal citing administrative convenience, but it was widely seen as a 'divide and rule' tactic against Indian nationalism.

questions.question: Who among the following foreign travellers is NOT correctly matched with their respective country they hail from?
questions.solution:
• Peter Mundy: Peter Mundy – China
  • Correction: Peter Mundy was an English traveler who visited India during the reign of Shah Jahan; he was not from China.

questions.question: Which of the following battles did Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah fight, defeating the forces under Henry Lawrence?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Chinhat: Battle of Chinhat
  • 1857: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah led the Indian forces to victory against the British at Chinhat during the Siege of Lucknow.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Cornwallis Code enacted?
questions.solution:
• Cornwallis Code: 1793
  • Legislation: This body of legislation provided for a separation of revenue and judicial functions in British Indian administration.
